v: The word of Yahweh[^1] that came to Micah of Moresheth[^2] in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah,[^3] which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֗ה אֶל־מִיכָה֙ הַמֹּ֣רַשְׁתִּ֔י בִּימֵ֥י יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖ה מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־חָזָ֥ה עַל־שֹׁמְר֖וֹן וִירֽוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Hear, you peoples, all of you;[^4] listen, earth, and all that is in it! Let the Lord Yahweh[^5] be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
שִׁמְעוּ֙ עַמִּ֣ים כֻּלָּ֔ם הַקְשִׁ֖יבִי אֶ֣רֶץ וּמְלֹאָ֑הּ וִיהִי֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֤ה בָּכֶם֙ לְעֵ֔ד אֲדֹנָ֖י מֵהֵיכַ֥ל קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
For look, Yahweh is coming out of his place. He will come down and tread on the heights of the earth.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה יֹצֵ֣א מִמְּקוֹמ֑וֹ וְיָרַ֥ד וְדָרַ֖ךְ עַל־*במותי **בָּ֥מֳתֵי אָֽרֶץ׃
The mountains will melt under him, and the valleys will split open, like wax before the fire, like water poured down a slope.
וְנָמַ֤סּוּ הֶֽהָרִים֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו וְהָעֲמָקִ֖ים יִתְבַּקָּ֑עוּ כַּדּוֹנַג֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָאֵ֔שׁ כְּמַ֖יִם מֻגָּרִ֥ים בְּמוֹרָֽד׃

All this is because of the rebellion[^6] of Jacob, because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the rebellion of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah?[^7] Are they not Jerusalem?
בְּפֶ֤שַׁע יַֽעֲקֹב֙ כָּל־זֹ֔את וּבְחַטֹּ֖אות בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִֽי־פֶ֣שַׁע יַעֲקֹ֗ב הֲלוֹא֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וּמִי֙ בָּמ֣וֹת יְהוּדָ֔ה הֲל֖וֹא יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
So I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open country, a place for planting vineyards. I will pour her stones down into the valley and lay bare her foundations.
וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י שֹׁמְר֛וֹן לְעִ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לְמַטָּ֣עֵי כָ֑רֶם וְהִגַּרְתִּ֤י לַגַּי֙ אֲבָנֶ֔יהָ וִיסֹדֶ֖יהָ אֲגַלֶּֽה׃

All her carved images will be smashed, all her prostitute's wages[^8] will be burned with fire, and I will make all her idols a desolation. For she gathered them from a prostitute's wages, and to a prostitute's wages they will return.
וְכָל־פְּסִילֶ֣יהָ יֻכַּ֗תּוּ וְכָל־אֶתְנַנֶּ֙יהָ֙ יִשָּׂרְפ֣וּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וְכָל־עֲצַבֶּ֖יהָ אָשִׂ֣ים שְׁמָמָ֑ה כִּ֠י מֵאֶתְנַ֤ן זוֹנָה֙ קִבָּ֔צָה וְעַד־אֶתְנַ֥ן זוֹנָ֖ה יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃
Because of this I will mourn and wail; I will go barefoot[^9] and naked. I will mourn like the jackals, and lament like the ostriches.
עַל־זֹאת֙ אֶסְפְּדָ֣ה וְאֵילִ֔ילָה אֵילְכָ֥ה *שילל **שׁוֹלָ֖ל וְעָר֑וֹם אֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה מִסְפֵּד֙ כַּתַּנִּ֔ים וְאֵ֖בֶל כִּבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃
For her wound is incurable;[^10] it has come to Judah. It has reached the gate of my people, Jerusalem itself.
כִּ֥י אֲנוּשָׁ֖ה מַכּוֹתֶ֑יהָ כִּי־בָ֙אָה֙ עַד־יְהוּדָ֔ה נָגַ֛ע עַד־שַׁ֥עַר עַמִּ֖י עַד־יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Tell it not in Gath;[^11] do not weep at all.[^12] In Beth-leaphrah, roll yourself in the dust.[^13]
בְּגַת֙ אַל־תַּגִּ֔ידוּ בָּכ֖וֹ אַל־תִּבְכּ֑וּ בְּבֵ֣ית לְעַפְרָ֔ה עָפָ֖ר *התפלשתי **הִתְפַּלָּֽשִׁי׃
Pass on your way, you who live in Shaphir, in shameful nakedness.[^14] Those who live in Zaanan do not come out.[^15] Beth-ezel is wailing; it will take its support away from you.[^16]
עִבְרִ֥י לָכֶ֛ם יוֹשֶׁ֥בֶת שָׁפִ֖יר עֶרְיָה־בֹ֑שֶׁת לֹ֤א יָֽצְאָה֙ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צַֽאֲנָ֔ן מִסְפַּד֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֵ֔צֶל יִקַּ֥ח מִכֶּ֖ם עֶמְדָּתֽוֹ׃
For those who live in Maroth writhe in anguish, waiting for good,[^17] because disaster has come down from Yahweh to the gate of Jerusalem.
כִּֽי־חָ֥לָֽה לְט֖וֹב יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת מָר֑וֹת כִּֽי־יָ֤רַד רָע֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לְשַׁ֖עַר יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Harness the horses to the chariot, you who live in Lachish.[^18] She was the beginning of sin for Daughter Zion,[^19] for in you were found the rebellions of Israel.
רְתֹ֧ם הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה לָרֶ֖כֶשׁ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָכִ֑ישׁ רֵאשִׁ֨ית חַטָּ֥את הִיא֙ לְבַת־צִיּ֔וֹן כִּי־בָ֥ךְ נִמְצְא֖וּ פִּשְׁעֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Therefore you will give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath.[^20] The houses of Achzib will be a deception to the kings of Israel.[^21]
לָכֵן֙ תִּתְּנִ֣י שִׁלּוּחִ֔ים עַ֖ל מוֹרֶ֣שֶׁת גַּ֑ת בָּתֵּ֤י אַכְזִיב֙ לְאַכְזָ֔ב לְמַלְכֵ֥[c]י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
I will yet bring a conqueror against you, you who live in Mareshah.[^22] The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.[^23]
עֹ֗ד הַיֹּרֵשׁ֙ אָ֣בִי לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת מָֽרֵשָׁ֑ה עַד־עֲדֻּלָּ֥ם יָב֖וֹא כְּב֥וֹד יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Shave your head bald and cut off your hair for the children you delight in. Make yourself as bald as the vulture,[^24] for they have gone from you into exile.
קָרְחִ֣י וָגֹ֔זִּי עַל־בְּנֵ֖י תַּעֲנוּגָ֑יִךְ הַרְחִ֤בִי קָרְחָתֵךְ֙ כַּנֶּ֔שֶׁר כִּ֥י גָל֖וּ מִמֵּֽךְ׃ ס

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: *Micah* is a short form of *Mikhayahu*, "Who is like Yahweh?" (compare 7:18). Moresheth, also called Moresheth-gath (verse 14), was a town in the low hills of Judah, about 25 miles (40 km) southwest of Jerusalem.
n.3: These kings reigned from about 750 to 686 BC. Jeremiah 26:18 quotes Micah 3:12 as spoken in the days of Hezekiah.
n.4: Literally "Hear, peoples, all of them". The same words end the story of the prophet Micaiah son of Imlah in 1 Kings 22:28.
n.5: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord Yahweh", traditionally "the Lord GOD". The second *Lord* in the verse is *Adonai* alone.
n.6: Hebrew *pesha*, "rebellion, transgression", a deliberate breaking of faith. Also in verse 13.
n.7: The high places were hill shrines where sacrifices were offered. The Septuagint reads "the sin of the house of Judah".
n.8: Hebrew *etnan*, the fee paid to a prostitute. The gifts given at Samaria's shrines are pictured as the earnings of an unfaithful wife (Hosea 2:14, 2:12 in most English Bibles; 9:1). When the city falls, its treasures will go to adorn the temples of the conquerors.
n.9: Or "stripped". The prophet acts out the fate of captives, as Isaiah did (Isaiah 20:2–4).
n.10: Literally "her wounds are incurable". *Her* is Samaria.
n.11: Verses 10–15 are a series of plays on the names of towns, most of them in the low hills of Judah near Micah's home, on the path of an invading army, probably that of Sennacherib king of Assyria in 701 BC. The Hebrew is difficult, and several of the towns are unknown. This line repeats David's lament for Saul (2 Samuel 1:20), and *Gath* (*gat*) sounds like *taggidu*, "tell".
n.12: Literally "weeping, do not weep". Some scholars read "In Acco do not weep", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.13: *Beth-leaphrah* means "house of dust", and *afar* is "dust". The Hebrew text is written "I have rolled myself" but read "roll yourself".
n.14: *Shaphir* means "beautiful", but its people will go into exile naked and ashamed. Literally "in nakedness of shame".
n.16: Literally "The wailing of Beth-ezel will take from you its standing place". The meaning is uncertain. *Beth-ezel* may mean "house nearby" or "house of removal".
n.17: *Maroth* means "bitterness". Its people hoped for good, but disaster came. Or "wait anxiously for good".
n.18: *Lachish*, the chief fortress of the low hills, sounds like *rekhesh*, "team of horses". Sennacherib besieged and took it in 701 BC (2 Kings 18:13–14).
n.19: A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman. Lachish may have been the first city in Judah to trust in chariots and horses, or to bring in the sins of the north.
n.20: Hebrew *shilluchim*, the gifts given to a daughter when she leaves home to be married. *Moresheth* sounds like *me'orasah*, "betrothed". Judah will have to give up Micah's home town as a father gives away his daughter.
n.21: *Achzib* sounds like *akhzav*, "deceptive", a word used of a stream that dries up (Jeremiah 15:18). *The kings of Israel* here may be the kings of Judah.
n.22: Hebrew *ha-yoresh*, "the one who takes possession", sounds like *Mareshah*.
n.23: The cave of Adullam was where David hid from Saul (1 Samuel 22:1). Israel's nobles, its *glory*, will have to hide there too.
n.24: Hebrew *nesher*, which can mean "eagle" or "vulture", here the griffon vulture, whose head and neck are almost bare. Shaving the head was a sign of mourning (Amos 8:10).

v: Woe to[^1] those who plan wickedness and work out evil on their beds! When morning dawns they carry it out, because it is in their power.[^2]
ה֧וֹי חֹֽשְׁבֵי־אָ֛וֶן וּפֹ֥עֲלֵי רָ֖ע עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם בְּא֤וֹר הַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ יַעֲשׂ֔וּהָ כִּ֥י יֶשׁ־לְאֵ֖ל יָדָֽם׃
They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and take them. They oppress a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.[^3]
וְחָמְד֤וּ שָׂדוֹת֙ וְגָזָ֔לוּ וּבָתִּ֖ים וְנָשָׂ֑אוּ וְעָֽשְׁקוּ֙ גֶּ֣בֶר וּבֵית֔וֹ וְאִ֖ישׁ וְנַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃ פ
Therefore this is what Yahweh[^4] says: Look, I am planning disaster against this clan, from which you cannot free your necks.[^5] You will no longer walk proudly, for it will be an evil time.[^6]
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י חֹשֵׁ֛ב עַל־הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את רָעָ֑ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־תָמִ֨ישׁוּ מִשָּׁ֜ם צַוְּארֹֽתֵיכֶ֗ם וְלֹ֤א תֵֽלְכוּ֙ רוֹמָ֔ה כִּ֛י עֵ֥ת רָעָ֖ה הִֽיא׃

On that day they will take up a taunt song[^7] against you and lament with a bitter lament,[^8] saying, "We are utterly ruined! He changes the portion of my people. How he takes it away from me! He divides our fields among traitors."[^9]
בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יִשָּׂ֧א עֲלֵיכֶ֣ם מָשָׁ֗ל וְנָהָ֨ה נְהִ֤י נִֽהְיָה֙ אָמַר֙ שָׁד֣וֹד נְשַׁדֻּ֔נוּ חֵ֥לֶק עַמִּ֖י יָמִ֑יר אֵ֚יךְ יָמִ֣ישׁ לִ֔י לְשׁוֹבֵ֥ב שָׂדֵ֖ינוּ יְחַלֵּֽק׃
Therefore you will have no one to cast the measuring line by lot[^10] in the assembly of Yahweh.
לָכֵן֙ לֹֽא־יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לְךָ֔ מַשְׁלִ֥יךְ חֶ֖בֶל בְּגוֹרָ֑ל בִּקְהַ֖ל יְהוָֽה׃
"Do not preach," they preach.[^11] "No one should preach about such things. Disgrace will not overtake us."[^12]
אַל־תַּטִּ֖פוּ יַטִּיפ֑וּן לֹֽא־יַטִּ֣פוּ לָאֵ֔לֶּה לֹ֥א יִסַּ֖ג כְּלִמּֽוֹת׃
Should this be said, house of Jacob?[^13] Is the Spirit of Yahweh impatient?[^14] Are these the things he does? Do not my words do good to the one who walks uprightly?
הֶאָמ֣וּר בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הֲקָצַר֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה אִם־אֵ֖לֶּה מַעֲלָלָ֑יו הֲל֤וֹא דְבָרַי֙ יֵיטִ֔יבוּ עִ֖ם הַיָּשָׁ֥ר הוֹלֵֽךְ׃
But lately my people have risen up as an enemy.[^15] You strip the robe from off the garment of those who pass by trustingly, like men returning from war.[^16]
וְאֶתְמ֗וּל עַמִּי֙ לְאוֹיֵ֣ב יְקוֹמֵ֔ם מִמּ֣וּל שַׂלְמָ֔ה אֶ֖דֶר תַּפְשִׁט֑וּן מֵעֹבְרִ֣ים בֶּ֔טַח שׁוּבֵ֖י מִלְחָמָֽה׃
You drive the women of my people out of the homes they delight in. From their young children you take away my splendor[^17] forever.
נְשֵׁ֤י עַמִּי֙ תְּגָ֣רְשׁ֔וּן מִבֵּ֖ית תַּֽעֲנֻגֶ֑יהָ מֵעַל֙ עֹֽלָלֶ֔יהָ תִּקְח֥וּ הֲדָרִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם׃
Get up and go, for this is no place of rest,[^18] because of the uncleanness that destroys with a painful destruction.[^19]
ק֣וּמוּ וּלְכ֔וּ כִּ֥י לֹא־זֹ֖את הַמְּנוּחָ֑ה בַּעֲב֥וּר טָמְאָ֛ה תְּחַבֵּ֖ל וְחֶ֥בֶל נִמְרָֽץ׃
If a man went about with wind and lies[^20] and deceived, saying, "I will preach to you about wine and beer," he would be the preacher for this people!
לוּ־אִ֞ישׁ הֹלֵ֥ךְ ר֙וּחַ֙ וָשֶׁ֣קֶר כִּזֵּ֔ב אַטִּ֣ף לְךָ֔ לַיַּ֖יִן וְלַשֵּׁכָ֑ר וְהָיָ֥ה מַטִּ֖יף הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely bring together the remnant of Israel. I will put them together like sheep in a fold,[^21] like a flock in the middle of its pasture. The place will hum with people.
אָסֹ֨ף אֶאֱסֹ֜ף יַעֲקֹ֣ב כֻּלָּ֗ךְ קַבֵּ֤ץ אֲקַבֵּץ֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֥חַד אֲשִׂימֶ֖נּוּ כְּצֹ֣אן בָּצְרָ֑ה כְּעֵ֙דֶר֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַדָּֽבְר֔וֹ תְּהִימֶ֖נָה מֵאָדָֽם׃
The one who breaks open the way[^22] will go up before them. They will break through, pass through the gate and go out by it. Their king will pass on before them, Yahweh at their head.
עָלָ֤ה הַפֹּרֵץ֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם פָּֽרְצוּ֙ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֔רוּ שַׁ֖עַר וַיֵּ֣צְאוּ ב֑וֹ וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר מַלְכָּם֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיהוָ֖ה בְּרֹאשָֽׁם׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning for the dead ("Alas!", 1 Kings 13:30). The prophets use it to announce disaster, and in that sense it is translated "Woe to" throughout this book.
n.2: Literally "because their hand is to God", an idiom for "it is within their power" (Genesis 31:29).
n.3: Hebrew *nachalah*, the family land handed down from one generation to the next (1 Kings 21:3).
n.4: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.5: The disaster is pictured as a yoke.
n.6: The same words are found in Amos 5:13.
n.7: Hebrew *mashal*, a saying or proverb, here a mocking song.
n.8: Literally "and lament a lament, 'It has happened,'", a play on similar-sounding words: *nahah nehi nihyah*.
n.9: Or "to the one who takes us captive". Hebrew *shovev*, "rebel, apostate". The Hebrew of the verse is difficult.
n.10: The land of Israel was first divided among its clans by lot (Joshua 14:2; 18:8–10). When the land is shared out again, the oppressors will have no share.
n.11: Literally "drip", as in Amos 7:16. Also in verse 11. The speakers are the people, or their prophets, who want to silence Micah.
n.12: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "They shall not drip to these; disgraces will not move away".
n.13: Some scholars read "Is the house of Jacob cursed?", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.14: Literally "Is the Spirit of Yahweh short?", that is, impatient or lacking in power (compare Numbers 11:23). Hebrew *ruach* can mean spirit, wind or breath.
n.15: The Hebrew is difficult. Some scholars read "But you rise up against my people as an enemy", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.16: Or "like men who are against war", peaceful people who expect no harm.
n.17: Perhaps their share in the land, or the freedom they had as Yahweh's people.
n.18: The promised land was to be Israel's place of rest (Deuteronomy 12:9).
n.19: Or "because it is unclean, it will be destroyed with a painful destruction". The Hebrew verb may also mean "take in pledge".
n.20: Hebrew *ruach*, "wind" or "spirit", the same word as in verse 7: a false prophet who claims the spirit but has only wind.
n.21: Hebrew *botsrah*, which is also the name Bozrah, a city of Edom, famous for its sheep (Isaiah 34:6).
n.22: Hebrew *ha-porets*, "the breaker", like a shepherd breaking open the gap in a sheepfold to lead the flock out.

v: And I said: Listen, you heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel! Is it not for you to know justice?
וָאֹמַ֗ר שִׁמְעוּ־נָא֙ רָאשֵׁ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּקְצִינֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֲל֣וֹא לָכֶ֔ם לָדַ֖עַת אֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
You hate good and love evil. You tear the skin off my people[^1] and the flesh off their bones.
שֹׂ֥נְאֵי ט֖וֹב וְאֹ֣הֲבֵי *רעה **רָ֑ע גֹּזְלֵ֤י עוֹרָם֙ מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וּשְׁאֵרָ֖ם מֵעַ֥ל עַצְמוֹתָֽם׃
You eat the flesh of my people and strip their skin off them. You break their bones in pieces and chop them up like meat for the pot,[^2] like flesh in a cauldron.
וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָכְלוּ֮ שְׁאֵ֣ר עַמִּי֒ וְעוֹרָם֙ מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֣ם הִפְשִׁ֔יטוּ וְאֶת־עַצְמֹֽתֵיהֶ֖ם פִּצֵּ֑חוּ וּפָרְשׂוּ֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּסִּ֔יר וּכְבָשָׂ֖ר בְּת֥וֹךְ קַלָּֽחַת׃
Then they will cry out to Yahweh,[^3] but he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time, because of the evil they have done.
אָ֚ז יִזְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יַעֲנֶ֖ה אוֹתָ֑ם וְיַסְתֵּ֨ר פָּנָ֤יו מֵהֶם֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵרֵ֖עוּ מַעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃ פ

This is what Yahweh says about the prophets who lead my people astray, who cry "Peace!" when they have something to bite with their teeth, but declare war[^4] on anyone who puts nothing in their mouths:
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים הַמַּתְעִ֣ים אֶת־עַמִּ֑י הַנֹּשְׁכִ֤ים בְּשִׁנֵּיהֶם֙ וְקָרְא֣וּ שָׁל֔וֹם וַאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹא־יִתֵּ֣ן עַל־פִּיהֶ֔ם וְקִדְּשׁ֥וּ עָלָ֖יו מִלְחָמָֽה׃
Therefore it will be night for you, with no vision, and darkness for you, with no divination.[^5] The sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will turn black over them.
לָכֵ֞ן לַ֤יְלָה לָכֶם֙ מֵֽחָז֔וֹן וְחָשְׁכָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם מִקְּסֹ֑ם וּבָ֤אָה הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ עַל־הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים וְקָדַ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃
The seers will be ashamed and the diviners disgraced. They will all cover their lips,[^6] because there is no answer from God.
וּבֹ֣שׁוּ הַחֹזִ֗ים וְחָֽפְרוּ֙ הַקֹּ֣סְמִ֔ים וְעָט֥וּ עַל־שָׂפָ֖ם כֻּלָּ֑ם כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין מַעֲנֵ֖ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃
But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of Yahweh,[^7] and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his rebellion and to Israel his sin.
וְאוּלָ֗ם אָנֹכִ֞י מָלֵ֤אתִי כֹ֙חַ֙ אֶת־ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּגְבוּרָ֑ה לְהַגִּ֤יד לְיַֽעֲקֹב֙ פִּשְׁע֔וֹ וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חַטָּאתֽוֹ׃ ס
Hear this, you heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who detest justice and twist everything that is straight,
שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֣א זֹ֗את רָאשֵׁי֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וּקְצִינֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הַֽמֲתַעֲבִ֣ים מִשְׁפָּ֔ט וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־הַיְשָׁרָ֖ה יְעַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃
who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.
בֹּנֶ֥ה צִיּ֖וֹן בְּדָמִ֑ים וִירוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם בְּעַוְלָֽה׃

Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach[^8] for a price, and her prophets practice divination for money. Yet they lean on Yahweh and say, "Is not Yahweh among us? No disaster will come on us."

רָאשֶׁ֣יהָ ׀ בְּשֹׁ֣חַד יִשְׁפֹּ֗טוּ וְכֹהֲנֶ֙יהָ֙ בִּמְחִ֣יר יוֹר֔וּ וּנְבִיאֶ֖יהָ בְּכֶ֣סֶף יִקְסֹ֑מוּ וְעַל־יְהוָה֙ יִשָּׁעֵ֣נוּ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֤וֹא יְהוָה֙ בְּקִרְבֵּ֔נוּ לֹֽא־תָב֥וֹא עָלֵ֖ינוּ רָעָֽה׃
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount a wooded height.[^9]
לָכֵן֙ בִּגְלַלְכֶ֔ם צִיּ֖וֹן שָׂדֶ֣ה תֵֽחָרֵ֑שׁ וִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עִיִּ֣ין תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְהַ֥ר הַבַּ֖יִת לְבָמ֥וֹת יָֽעַר׃ פ

n.1: Literally "their skin from on them". *My people* is supplied from verse 3.
n.2: Literally "spread them out as in a pot". Some scholars read "like flesh in a pot", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "consecrate war", as for a holy war.
n.5: Hebrew *qesem*, the reading of omens, forbidden in Deuteronomy 18:10. Micah uses it with scorn of the prophets' practice. Also in verses 7 and 11.
n.6: Literally "cover the mustache", a sign of shame or mourning (Leviticus 13:45; Ezekiel 24:17, 22).
n.7: Or "by the Spirit of Yahweh". Hebrew *ruach* can mean spirit, wind or breath.
n.8: Hebrew *yoru*, the verb from which *torah*, "instruction", comes. The priests were to teach the people Yahweh's instruction (Deuteronomy 33:10; Malachi 2:7).
n.9: *The temple mount* is literally "the mountain of the house". Jeremiah 26:18 quotes this verse about a century later, as spoken in the days of Hezekiah.

v: In the days to come,[^1] the mountain of Yahweh's[^2] house will be established as the highest of the mountains;[^3] it will be raised above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.[^4]
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים יִ֠הְיֶה הַ֣ר בֵּית־יְהוָ֤ה נָכוֹן֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הֶהָרִ֔ים וְנִשָּׂ֥א ה֖וּא מִגְּבָע֑וֹת וְנָהֲר֥וּ עָלָ֖יו עַמִּֽים׃

Many nations will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob, so that he may teach us his ways and we may walk in his paths." For instruction[^5] will go out from Zion, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.

וְֽהָלְכ֞וּ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֗ים וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ לְכ֣וּ ׀ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה אֶל־הַר־יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶל־בֵּית֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיוֹרֵ֙נוּ֙ מִדְּרָכָ֔יו וְנֵלְכָ֖ה בְּאֹֽרְחֹתָ֑יו כִּ֤י מִצִיּוֹן֙ תֵּצֵ֣א תוֹרָ֔ה וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה מִירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for strong nations far away. They will beat their swords into plowshares[^6] and their spears into pruning knives. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not learn war anymore.

וְשָׁפַ֗ט בֵּ֚ין עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וְהוֹכִ֛יחַ לְגוֹיִ֥ם עֲצֻמִ֖ים עַד־רָח֑וֹק וְכִתְּת֨וּ חַרְבֹתֵיהֶ֜ם לְאִתִּ֗ים וַחֲנִיתֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ לְמַזְמֵר֔וֹת לֹֽא־יִשְׂא֞וּ גּ֤וֹי אֶל־גּוֹי֙ חֶ֔רֶב וְלֹא־יִלְמְד֥וּן ע֖וֹד מִלְחָמָֽה׃
Each of them will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and no one will make them afraid,[^7] for the mouth of Yahweh of Armies[^8] has spoken.
וְיָשְׁב֗וּ אִ֣ישׁ תַּ֧חַת גַּפְנ֛וֹ וְתַ֥חַת תְּאֵנָת֖וֹ וְאֵ֣ין מַחֲרִ֑יד כִּי־פִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת דִּבֵּֽר׃
For all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of Yahweh our God forever and ever.
כִּ֚י כָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים יֵלְכ֕וּ אִ֖ישׁ בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ נֵלֵ֛ךְ בְּשֵׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃ פ
On that day, declares Yahweh,[^9] I will gather the lame[^10] and bring together those who have been driven away, those whom I have afflicted.
בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה אֹֽסְפָה֙ הַצֹּ֣לֵעָ֔ה וְהַנִּדָּחָ֖ה אֲקַבֵּ֑צָה וַאֲשֶׁ֖ר הֲרֵעֹֽתִי׃
I will make the lame a remnant, and those driven far away[^11] a strong nation. Yahweh will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever.
וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י אֶת־הַצֹּֽלֵעָה֙ לִשְׁאֵרִ֔ית וְהַנַּהֲלָאָ֖ה לְג֣וֹי עָצ֑וּם וּמָלַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֤ה עֲלֵיהֶם֙ בְּהַ֣ר צִיּ֔וֹן מֵעַתָּ֖ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃ פ
And you, watchtower of the flock,[^12] stronghold of Daughter Zion,[^13] to you it will come: the former dominion will come, the kingdom of Daughter Jerusalem.
וְאַתָּ֣ה מִגְדַּל־עֵ֗דֶר עֹ֛פֶל בַּת־צִיּ֖וֹן עָדֶ֣יךָ תֵּאתֶ֑ה וּבָאָ֗ה הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה מַמְלֶ֖כֶת לְבַ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?
עַתָּ֕ה לָ֥מָּה תָרִ֖יעִי רֵ֑עַ הֲמֶ֣לֶךְ אֵֽין־בָּ֗ךְ אִֽם־יוֹעֲצֵךְ֙ אָבָ֔ד כִּֽי־הֶחֱזִיקֵ֥ךְ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃

Writhe and groan,[^14] Daughter Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you will go out from the city and camp in the open country. You will go to Babylon.[^15] There you will be rescued; there Yahweh will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
ח֧וּלִי וָגֹ֛חִי בַּת־צִיּ֖וֹן כַּיּֽוֹלֵדָ֑ה כִּֽי־עַתָּה֩ תֵצְאִ֨י מִקִּרְיָ֜ה וְשָׁכַ֣נְתְּ בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה וּבָ֤את עַד־בָּבֶל֙ שָׁ֣ם תִּנָּצֵ֔לִי שָׁ֚ם יִגְאָלֵ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה מִכַּ֖ף אֹיְבָֽיִךְ׃
But now many nations have gathered against you. They say, "Let her be defiled,[^16] and let our eyes gloat over Zion."
וְעַתָּ֛ה נֶאֶסְפ֥וּ עָלַ֖יִךְ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֑ים הָאֹמְרִ֣ים תֶּחֱנָ֔ף וְתַ֥חַז בְּצִיּ֖וֹן עֵינֵֽינוּ׃
But they do not know the thoughts of Yahweh, and they do not understand his plan: he has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.
וְהֵ֗מָּה לֹ֤א יָֽדְעוּ֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א הֵבִ֖ינוּ עֲצָת֑וֹ כִּ֥י קִבְּצָ֖ם כֶּעָמִ֥יר גֹּֽרְנָה׃

Rise and thresh, Daughter Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you will crush many peoples. You will devote[^17] their plunder to Yahweh, their wealth to the Lord of the whole earth.

ק֧וּמִי וָד֣וֹשִׁי בַת־צִיּ֗וֹן כִּֽי־קַרְנֵ֞ךְ אָשִׂ֤ים בַּרְזֶל֙ וּפַרְסֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ אָשִׂ֣ים נְחוּשָׁ֔ה וַהֲדִקּ֖וֹת עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְהַחֲרַמְתִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ בִּצְעָ֔ם וְחֵילָ֖ם לַאֲד֥וֹן כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Now gather your troops, daughter of troops![^18] A siege has been laid against us. With a rod they will strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.[^19]
עַתָּה֙ תִּתְגֹּדְדִ֣י בַת־גְּד֔וּד מָצ֖וֹר שָׂ֣ם עָלֵ֑ינוּ בַּשֵּׁ֙בֶט֙ יַכּ֣וּ עַֽל־הַלְּחִ֔י אֵ֖ת שֹׁפֵ֥ט יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס

n.1: Literally "at the end of the days". Verses 1–3 are found also in Isaiah 2:2–4, with small differences. Verse 4 is found only in Micah.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "at the head of the mountains".
n.4: Or "will flow to it", like a river.
n.6: Hebrew *ittim*, probably iron plow points or hoes. Joel 4:10 (3:10 in most English Bibles) turns the image around: "Beat your plowshares into swords."
n.7: A picture of peace and safety, as in the days of Solomon (1 Kings 5:5, 4:25 in most English Bibles; compare Zechariah 3:10).
n.8: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.9: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of Yahweh", a formula that marks a prophet's words as Yahweh's own solemn statement.
n.10: The Hebrew is feminine singular, "the limping one", picturing the people as a lame ewe of the flock. Also in verse 7. Compare Zephaniah 3:19.
n.11: Hebrew *ha-nahala'ah*, found only here. Perhaps "those cast far off".
n.12: Hebrew *Migdal-eder*, a shepherd's tower for watching over the flock. Genesis 35:21 names a place near Bethlehem by it. Here it is Jerusalem.
n.13: Hebrew *ophel*, "mound, stronghold", also the name of the hill of the City of David, south of the temple (2 Chronicles 27:3). *Daughter Zion* is a poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman.
n.14: The meaning of the second verb is uncertain. Perhaps "push" or "burst out", as in giving birth.
n.15: In Micah's time Assyria was the great power. Babylon became the leading power about a century later, and took the people of Judah into exile there (compare 2 Kings 20:12–18).
n.17: Hebrew *ve-hacharamti*, which usually means "I will devote", but is probably here an old form of "you will devote". To devote something was to give it wholly to God, often by destroying it (Joshua 6:17–19).
n.18: The meaning is uncertain. The verb can mean "gash yourself", a mourning rite (Jeremiah 16:6), or "gather in bands". Here it plays on *gedud*, "troop, raiding band". Verse 14 is 5:1 in most English Bibles.
n.19: The *judge of Israel* is its ruler. *Judge* (*shofet*) sounds like *shevet*, "rod".

v: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah,[^1] too small to be among the clans[^2] of Judah, from you one will come out for me to be ruler in Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient days.[^3]
וְאַתָּ֞ה בֵּֽית־לֶ֣חֶם אֶפְרָ֗תָה צָעִיר֙ לִֽהְיוֹת֙ בְּאַלְפֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה מִמְּךָ֙ לִ֣י יֵצֵ֔א לִֽהְי֥וֹת מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמוֹצָאֹתָ֥יו מִקֶּ֖דֶם מִימֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
Therefore he will give them up until the time when she who is in labor has given birth.[^4] Then the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
לָכֵ֣ן יִתְּנֵ֔ם עַד־עֵ֥ת יוֹלֵדָ֖ה יָלָ֑דָה וְיֶ֣תֶר אֶחָ֔יו יְשׁוּב֖וּן עַל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
He will stand and shepherd his flock[^5] in the strength of Yahweh,[^6] in the majesty of the name of Yahweh his God. And they will live secure, for now he will be great to the ends of the earth.
וְעָמַ֗ד וְרָעָה֙ בְּעֹ֣ז יְהוָ֔ה בִּגְא֕וֹן שֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וְיָשָׁ֕בוּ כִּֽי־עַתָּ֥ה יִגְדַּ֖ל עַד־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
And he will be our peace.[^7] When Assyria comes into our land and treads on our fortresses, we will raise up against it seven shepherds, eight leaders of men.[^8]
וְהָיָ֥ה זֶ֖ה שָׁל֑וֹם אַשּׁ֣וּר ׀ כִּֽי־יָב֣וֹא בְאַרְצֵ֗נוּ וְכִ֤י יִדְרֹךְ֙ בְּאַרְמְנֹתֵ֔ינוּ וַהֲקֵמֹ֤נוּ עָלָיו֙ שִׁבְעָ֣ה רֹעִ֔ים וּשְׁמֹנָ֖ה נְסִיכֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
They will shepherd[^9] the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod[^10] at its gates.[^11] He will rescue us from Assyria when it comes into our land and treads within our borders.
וְרָע֞וּ אֶת־אֶ֤רֶץ אַשּׁוּר֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶב וְאֶת־אֶ֥רֶץ נִמְרֹ֖ד בִּפְתָחֶ֑יהָ וְהִצִּיל֙ מֵֽאַשּׁ֔וּר כִּֽי־יָב֣וֹא בְאַרְצֵ֔נוּ וְכִ֥י יִדְרֹ֖ךְ בִּגְבוּלֵֽנוּ׃ ס
The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from Yahweh, like showers on the grass, which do not wait for anyone or depend on human beings.[^12]
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֗ב בְּקֶ֙רֶב֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים כְּטַל֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כִּרְבִיבִ֖ים עֲלֵי־עֵ֑שֶׂב אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יְקַוֶּה֙ לְאִ֔ישׁ וְלֹ֥א יְיַחֵ֖ל לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃

The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, among many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which tramples and tears as it goes, and there is no one to rescue.
וְהָיָה֩ שְׁאֵרִ֨ית יַעֲקֹ֜ב בַּגּוֹיִ֗ם בְּקֶ֙רֶב֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים כְּאַרְיֵה֙ בְּבַהֲמ֣וֹת יַ֔עַר כִּכְפִ֖יר בְּעֶדְרֵי[c] צֹ֑אן אֲשֶׁ֧ר אִם[c] עָבַ֛ר וְרָמַ֥ס וְטָרַ֖ף וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃
Your hand will be raised over your adversaries, and all your enemies will be cut off.
תָּרֹ֥ם יָדְךָ֖ עַל־צָרֶ֑יךָ וְכָל־אֹיְבֶ֖יךָ יִכָּרֵֽתוּ׃ פ
On that day, declares Yahweh,[^13] I will cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
וְהָיָ֤ה בַיּוֹם־הַהוּא֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י סוּסֶ֖יךָ מִקִּרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖י מַרְכְּבֹתֶֽיךָ׃
I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.
וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י עָרֵ֣י אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וְהָרַסְתִּ֖י כָּל־מִבְצָרֶֽיךָ׃
I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you will have no more fortune-tellers.[^14]
וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י כְשָׁפִ֖ים מִיָּדֶ֑ךָ וּֽמְעוֹנְנִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִֽהְיוּ־לָֽךְ׃
I will cut off your carved images and your standing stones[^15] from among you, and you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
וְהִכְרַתִּ֧י פְסִילֶ֛יךָ וּמַצֵּבוֹתֶ֖יךָ מִקִּרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה ע֖וֹד לְמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ׃
I will uproot your Asherah poles[^16] from among you and destroy your cities.[^17]
וְנָתַשְׁתִּ֥י אֲשֵׁירֶ֖יךָ מִקִּרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְהִשְׁמַדְתִּ֖י עָרֶֽיךָ׃
In anger and wrath I will take vengeance on the nations that have not obeyed.[^18]
וְעָשִׂ֜יתִי בְּאַ֧ף וּבְחֵמָ֛ה נָקָ֖ם אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א שָׁמֵֽעוּ׃ ס

n.1: Verses 1–14 are 5:2–15 in most English Bibles. Bethlehem, also called Ephrathah, was the home town of David (Ruth 4:11; 1 Samuel 17:12). Matthew 2:6 quotes this verse freely, together with words from 2 Samuel 5:2: "And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah, for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel." Compare John 7:42.
n.2: Literally "the thousands", the clans that each provided a unit of soldiers. The same consonants can be read "the chiefs", as in Matthew's "among the rulers of Judah".
n.3: Or "from days long ago". *Origins* is literally "goings out".
n.4: Perhaps the mother of the coming ruler (compare Isaiah 7:14), or Zion in her labor pains (4:9–10).
n.5: *His flock* is added. Literally "He will stand and shepherd".
n.6: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.7: Or "This will be our peace". Literally "This one will be peace".
n.8: A number saying, as in Amos 1:3: as many leaders as are needed, and more.
n.9: The verb *ra'ah*, "shepherd", can also be read *ra'a'*, "shatter".
n.10: The mighty hunter, founder of cities in Babylonia and Assyria (Genesis 10:8–12).
n.11: Literally "in its entrances". Some scholars read "with the drawn sword", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.12: Dew and rain come from Yahweh alone, not from human effort.
n.13: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of Yahweh", a formula that marks a prophet's words as Yahweh's own solemn statement.
n.14: Practices forbidden in Deuteronomy 18:10–14. *Fortune-tellers* is Hebrew *me'onenim*, a word of uncertain meaning.
n.15: Hebrew *matsevot*, stone pillars set up at places of worship, forbidden in Deuteronomy 16:22.
n.16: Hebrew *asherim*, wooden poles or trees that were symbols of the goddess Asherah (Deuteronomy 16:21).
n.17: Some scholars read "your idols", with a small change to the Hebrew.

v: Hear what Yahweh[^1] is saying: Rise, plead your case[^2] before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֕א אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֖ה אֹמֵ֑ר ק֚וּם רִ֣יב אֶת־הֶהָרִ֔ים וְתִשְׁמַ֥עְנָה הַגְּבָע֖וֹת קוֹלֶֽךָ׃
Hear, you mountains, Yahweh's case, you enduring foundations of the earth! For Yahweh has a case against his people, and he will argue it with Israel.
שִׁמְע֤וּ הָרִים֙ אֶת־רִ֣יב יְהוָ֔ה וְהָאֵתָנִ֖ים מֹ֣סְדֵי אָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י רִ֤יב לַֽיהוָה֙ עִם־עַמּ֔וֹ וְעִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִתְוַכָּֽח׃
My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you?[^3] Answer me!
עַמִּ֛י מֶה־עָשִׂ֥יתִי לְךָ֖ וּמָ֣ה הֶלְאֵתִ֑יךָ עֲנֵ֥ה בִּֽי׃
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam ahead of you.
כִּ֤י הֶעֱלִתִ֙יךָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִ֖ים פְּדִיתִ֑יךָ וָאֶשְׁלַ֣ח לְפָנֶ֔יךָ אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה אַהֲרֹ֥ן וּמִרְיָֽם׃
My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned and what Balaam son of Beor answered him,[^4] and what happened from Shittim to Gilgal,[^5] so that you may know the saving acts[^6] of Yahweh.
עַמִּ֗י זְכָר־נָא֙ מַה־יָּעַ֗ץ בָּלָק֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב וּמֶה־עָנָ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ בִּלְעָ֣ם בֶּן־בְּע֑וֹר מִן־הַשִּׁטִּים֙ עַד־הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל לְמַ֕עַן דַּ֖עַת צִדְק֥וֹת יְהוָֽה׃
"With what shall I come before Yahweh[^7] and bow down before God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
בַּמָּה֙ אֲקַדֵּ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה אִכַּ֖ף לֵאלֹהֵ֣י מָר֑וֹם הַאֲקַדְּמֶ֣נּוּ בְעוֹל֔וֹת בַּעֲגָלִ֖ים בְּנֵ֥י שָׁנָֽה׃
Will Yahweh be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my rebellion, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?"[^8]
הֲיִרְצֶ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּאַלְפֵ֣י אֵילִ֔ים בְּרִֽבְב֖וֹת נַֽחֲלֵי־שָׁ֑מֶן הַאֶתֵּ֤ן בְּכוֹרִי֙ פִּשְׁעִ֔י פְּרִ֥י בִטְנִ֖י חַטַּ֥את נַפְשִֽׁי׃
He has told you, mortal,[^9] what is good. And what does Yahweh require of you but to do justice, to love faithful love,[^10] and to walk humbly[^11] with your God?
הִגִּ֥יד לְךָ֛ אָדָ֖ם מַה־טּ֑וֹב וּמָֽה־יְהוָ֞ה דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ מִמְּךָ֗ כִּ֣י אִם־עֲשׂ֤וֹת מִשְׁפָּט֙ וְאַ֣הֲבַת חֶ֔סֶד וְהַצְנֵ֥עַ לֶ֖כֶת עִם־אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃ פ
Listen! Yahweh is calling to the city, and it is wisdom to fear your name:[^12] Hear of the rod, and of the one who appointed it.[^13]
ק֤וֹל יְהוָה֙ לָעִ֣יר יִקְרָ֔א וְתוּשִׁיָּ֖ה יִרְאֶ֣ה שְׁמֶ֑ךָ שִׁמְע֥וּ מַטֶּ֖ה וּמִ֥י יְעָדָֽהּ׃
Can I forget[^14] the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the short ephah,[^15] which is cursed?
ע֗וֹד הַאִשׁ֙ בֵּ֣ית רָשָׁ֔ע אֹצְר֖וֹת רֶ֑שַׁע וְאֵיפַ֥ת רָז֖וֹן זְעוּמָֽה׃
Can I acquit[^16] someone with wicked scales, with a bag of false weights?
הַאֶזְכֶּ֖ה בְּמֹ֣אזְנֵי רֶ֑שַׁע וּבְכִ֖יס אַבְנֵ֥י מִרְמָֽה׃
Her rich men are full of violence; her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues in their mouths are deceitful.
אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֲשִׁירֶ֙יהָ֙ מָלְא֣וּ חָמָ֔ס וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ דִּבְּרוּ־שָׁ֑קֶר וּלְשׁוֹנָ֖ם רְמִיָּ֥ה בְּפִיהֶֽם׃
So I have struck you with a painful wound,[^17] to make you desolate because of your sins.
וְגַם־אֲנִ֖י הֶחֱלֵ֣יתִי הַכּוֹתֶ֑ךָ הַשְׁמֵ֖ם עַל־חַטֹּאתֶֽךָ׃
You will eat but not be satisfied; your hunger[^18] will remain inside you. You will carry things away but not save them,[^19] and what you do save I will give to the sword.
אַתָּ֤ה תֹאכַל֙ וְלֹ֣א תִשְׂבָּ֔ע וְיֶשְׁחֲךָ֖ בְּקִרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְתַסֵּג֙ וְלֹ֣א תַפְלִ֔יט וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּפַלֵּ֖ט לַחֶ֥רֶב אֶתֵּֽן׃
You will sow but not reap; you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil, and tread grapes[^20] but not drink wine.
אַתָּ֥ה תִזְרַ֖ע וְלֹ֣א תִקְצ֑וֹר אַתָּ֤ה תִדְרֹֽךְ־זַ֙יִת֙ וְלֹא־תָס֣וּךְ שֶׁ֔מֶן וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁתֶּה־יָּֽיִן׃

For the decrees of Omri are kept, and all the practices of the house of Ahab,[^21] and you have followed their advice. So I will make you a desolation, and the city's inhabitants an object of hissing;[^22] you will bear the scorn of my people.[^23]
וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּ֞ר חֻקּ֣וֹת עָמְרִ֗י וְכֹל֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה בֵית־אַחְאָ֔ב וַתֵּלְכ֖וּ בְּמֹֽעֲצוֹתָ֑ם לְמַעַן֩ תִּתִּ֨י אֹתְךָ֜ לְשַׁמָּ֗ה וְיֹשְׁבֶ֙יהָ֙ לִשְׁרֵקָ֔ה וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת עַמִּ֖י תִּשָּֽׂאוּ׃ פ

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *riv*, a lawsuit. Yahweh brings a case against his people, with the mountains and the foundations of the earth as witnesses (compare Deuteronomy 32:1; Isaiah 1:2). Also in verse 2.
n.3: A play on words: *he'le'tikha*, "I have wearied you", and *he'elitikha*, "I brought you up", in verse 4.
n.4: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, but Balaam blessed them instead (Numbers 22–24).
n.5: Shittim was Israel's last camp east of the Jordan (Numbers 25:1; Joshua 3:1), and Gilgal the first camp west of it, after the crossing (Joshua 4:19). *What happened* is added: literally "from Shittim to Gilgal".
n.6: Hebrew *tsidqot*, "righteous acts", here Yahweh's acts of rescue (Judges 5:11).
n.7: In verses 6–7 a worshiper asks what Yahweh wants, and in verse 8 the prophet answers.
n.8: Hebrew *nephesh*, "soul, self, life". The sacrifice of children was forbidden and condemned (Leviticus 18:21; 2 Kings 16:3; 21:6).
n.10: Hebrew *chesed*, loyal, covenant love, shown to God and to others. Traditionally "to love mercy" or "to love kindness".
n.11: Or "carefully", "wisely". The meaning of the Hebrew word, *hatsnea*, is not certain. This verse is often taken as a summary of the prophets' teaching (compare Isaiah 1:17; Hosea 6:6; Amos 5:24).
n.12: The Hebrew of verses 9–10 is difficult. Literally "and wisdom sees your name". The same consonants can be read "fear your name". The Septuagint reads "and he will save those who fear his name".
n.13: The rod of punishment (Isaiah 10:5). Or "Hear, you tribe, and the one who assembled it". Hebrew *matteh* can mean "rod" or "tribe".
n.14: Literally "Is there yet a man of the house of the wicked …?" Many scholars read "Can I forget …?", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.15: Literally "the ephah of leanness": a measure made smaller than it should be, to cheat the buyer (Amos 8:5). An ephah was probably about 22 liters (two-thirds of a bushel).
n.16: Literally "Shall I be pure with …?" The same consonants can be read "Shall I acquit …?"
n.17: Literally "I have made sick, striking you". The Septuagint reads "I will begin to strike you".
n.18: Hebrew *yeshach*, found only here. The meaning is uncertain: perhaps "emptiness".
n.19: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.20: Hebrew *tirosh*, new wine, the fresh juice of the grapes.
n.21: Omri and his son Ahab, kings of Israel in the ninth century BC, built Samaria and promoted the worship of Baal. Ahab took Naboth's vineyard by fraud and murder (1 Kings 16:23–33; 21).
n.22: People whistled in horror at the sight of a ruin (Jeremiah 19:8). *The city's inhabitants* is literally "her inhabitants".
n.23: The Septuagint reads "the scorn of peoples".

v: Woe is me![^1] For I have become like one who gathers summer fruit, like one who gleans after the grape harvest. There is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I[^2] long for.
אַ֣לְלַי לִ֗י כִּ֤י הָיִ֙יתִי֙ כְּאָסְפֵּי־קַ֔יִץ כְּעֹלְלֹ֖ת בָּצִ֑יר אֵין־אֶשְׁכּ֣וֹל לֶאֱכ֔וֹל בִּכּוּרָ֖ה אִוְּתָ֥ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃
The faithful[^3] have vanished from the land, and there is no one upright among human beings. All of them lie in wait to shed blood; each hunts his brother with a net.
אָבַ֤ד חָסִיד֙ מִן־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְיָשָׁ֥ר בָּאָדָ֖ם אָ֑יִן כֻּלָּם֙ לְדָמִ֣ים יֶאֱרֹ֔בוּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִ֖יהוּ יָצ֥וּדוּ חֵֽרֶם׃
Their hands are skilled at doing evil.[^4] The official asks for gifts, and the judge judges for a bribe. The powerful man speaks out what he craves, and so they weave it together.[^5]
עַל־הָרַ֤ע כַּפַּ֙יִם֙ לְהֵיטִ֔יב הַשַּׂ֣ר שֹׁאֵ֔ל וְהַשֹּׁפֵ֖ט בַּשִׁלּ֑וּם וְהַגָּד֗וֹל דֹּבֵ֨ר הַוַּ֥ת נַפְשׁ֛וֹ ה֖וּא וַֽיְעַבְּתֽוּהָ׃
The best of them is like a briar, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen,[^6] the day of your punishment, has come; now their confusion will come.
טוֹבָ֣ם כְּחֵ֔דֶק יָשָׁ֖ר מִמְּסוּכָ֑ה י֤וֹם מְצַפֶּ֙יךָ֙ פְּקֻדָּתְךָ֣ בָ֔אָה עַתָּ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה מְבוּכָתָֽם׃
Do not trust a neighbor; do not rely on a friend. Guard the doors of your mouth from the woman who lies in your arms.
אַל־תַּאֲמִ֣ינוּ בְרֵ֔עַ אַֽל־תִּבְטְח֖וּ בְּאַלּ֑וּף מִשֹּׁכֶ֣בֶת חֵיקֶ֔ךָ שְׁמֹ֖ר פִּתְחֵי־פִֽיךָ׃
For the son treats his father with contempt, the daughter rises up against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man's enemies are the people of his own household.[^7]
כִּֽי־בֵן֙ מְנַבֵּ֣ל אָ֔ב בַּ֚ת קָמָ֣ה בְאִמָּ֔הּ כַּלָּ֖ה בַּחֲמֹתָ֑הּ אֹיְבֵ֥י אִ֖ישׁ אַנְשֵׁ֥י בֵיתֽוֹ׃
But as for me, I will watch for Yahweh;[^8] I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
וַאֲנִי֙ בַּיהוָ֣ה אֲצַפֶּ֔ה אוֹחִ֖ילָה לֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעִ֑י יִשְׁמָעֵ֖נִי אֱלֹהָֽי׃
Do not gloat over me, my enemy![^9] Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, Yahweh is my light.
אַֽל־תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י אֹיַ֙בְתִּי֙ לִ֔י כִּ֥י נָפַ֖לְתִּי קָ֑מְתִּי כִּֽי־אֵשֵׁ֣ב בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ יְהוָ֖ה א֥וֹר לִֽי׃ ס
I will bear the anger of Yahweh, because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and gives me justice. He will bring me out into the light; I will see his righteousness.[^10]
זַ֤עַף יְהוָה֙ אֶשָּׂ֔א כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אתִי ל֑וֹ עַד֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֤יב רִיבִי֙ וְעָשָׂ֣ה מִשְׁפָּטִ֔י יוֹצִיאֵ֣נִי לָא֔וֹר אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּצִדְקָתֽוֹ׃
Then my enemy will see it, and shame will cover her, she who said to me, "Where is Yahweh your God?" My eyes will look on her; now she will be trampled down like mud in the streets.
וְתֵרֶ֤א אֹיַ֙בְתִּי֙ וּתְכַסֶּ֣הָ בוּשָׁ֔ה הָאֹמְרָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י אַיּ֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יִךְ עֵינַי֙ תִּרְאֶ֣ינָּה בָּ֔הּ עַתָּ֛ה תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה לְמִרְמָ֖ס כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃
A day for building your walls! On that day the boundary will be extended far.[^11]
י֖וֹם לִבְנ֣וֹת גְּדֵרָ֑יִךְ י֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יִרְחַק־חֹֽק׃
On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt,[^12] from Egypt to the River,[^13] from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
י֥וֹם הוּא֙ וְעָדֶ֣יךָ יָב֔וֹא לְמִנִּ֥י אַשּׁ֖וּר וְעָרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר וּלְמִנִּ֤י מָצוֹר֙ וְעַד־נָהָ֔ר וְיָ֥ם מִיָּ֖ם וְהַ֥ר הָהָֽר׃
But the earth will become a desolation because of those who live in it, as the fruit of their deeds.
וְהָיְתָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ לִשְׁמָמָ֖ה עַל־יֹֽשְׁבֶ֑יהָ מִפְּרִ֖י מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃ ס

Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock that is your inheritance, which lives alone in a forest in the middle of a fruitful land.[^14] Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead[^15] as in the days of old.
רְעֵ֧ה עַמְּךָ֣ בְשִׁבְטֶ֗ךָ צֹ֚אן נַֽחֲלָתֶ֔ךָ שֹׁכְנִ֣י לְבָדָ֔ד יַ֖עַר בְּת֣וֹךְ כַּרְמֶ֑ל יִרְע֥וּ בָשָׁ֛ן וְגִלְעָ֖ד כִּימֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show them wonders.[^16]
כִּימֵ֥י צֵאתְךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אַרְאֶ֖נּוּ נִפְלָאֽוֹת׃
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might. They will put their hands over their mouths; their ears will be deaf.
יִרְא֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ וְיֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מִכֹּ֖ל גְּבֽוּרָתָ֑ם יָשִׂ֤ימוּ יָד֙ עַל־פֶּ֔ה אָזְנֵיהֶ֖ם תֶּחֱרַֽשְׁנָה׃

They will lick the dust like a snake, like creatures that crawl on the ground. They will come trembling out of their strongholds. They will turn in fear to Yahweh our God, and they will be afraid of you.
יְלַחֲכ֤וּ עָפָר֙ כַּנָּחָ֔שׁ כְּזֹחֲלֵ֣י אֶ֔רֶץ יִרְגְּז֖וּ מִמִּסְגְּרֹֽתֵיהֶ֑ם אֶל־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ יִפְחָ֔דוּ וְיִֽרְא֖וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

Who is a God like you,[^17] who forgives wrongdoing and passes over the rebellion of the remnant of his inheritance? He does not hold on to his anger forever, because he delights in faithful love.[^18]
מִי־אֵ֣ל כָּמ֗וֹךָ נֹשֵׂ֤א עָוֺן֙ וְעֹבֵ֣ר עַל־פֶּ֔שַׁע לִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית נַחֲלָת֑וֹ לֹא־הֶחֱזִ֤יק לָעַד֙ אַפּ֔וֹ כִּֽי־חָפֵ֥ץ חֶ֖סֶד הֽוּא׃
He will again have compassion on us; he will tread our wrongdoings underfoot. You will hurl all their sins[^19] into the depths of the sea.
יָשׁ֣וּב יְרַֽחֲמֵ֔נוּ יִכְבֹּ֖שׁ עֲוֺֽנֹתֵ֑ינוּ וְתַשְׁלִ֛יךְ בִּמְצֻל֥וֹת יָ֖ם כָּל־חַטֹּאותָֽם׃
You will show faithfulness to Jacob and faithful love to Abraham,[^20] as you swore to our ancestors in the days of old.
תִּתֵּ֤ן אֱמֶת֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב חֶ֖סֶד לְאַבְרָהָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתָּ לַאֲבֹתֵ֖ינוּ מִ֥ימֵי קֶֽדֶם׃

n.1: Hebrew *alelai li*, a cry of grief, found also in Job 10:15.
n.4: Literally "On evil, both hands, to do it well".
n.5: The meaning of the last words is uncertain. Literally "he, and they weave it".
n.6: The prophets, who watched and warned of the coming day (Jeremiah 6:17; Ezekiel 3:17).
n.7: Jesus echoes this verse in Matthew 10:35–36 and Luke 12:53.
n.8: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.9: The Hebrew is feminine. In verses 8–10 Zion speaks to an enemy city or nation, and in verses 11–13 she is addressed.
n.10: Or "his saving justice". Hebrew *tsedaqah*, "righteousness", here Yahweh's faithfulness in putting things right.
n.11: Hebrew *choq*, "boundary" or "decree". Or "the decree will be far off".
n.12: Hebrew *matsor*, a rare poetic name for Egypt (2 Kings 19:24; Isaiah 19:6), which also means "siege" or "fortress". Also later in the verse.
n.14: Hebrew *karmel*, "garden land, orchard", also the name of Mount Carmel (Amos 1:2).
n.15: Rich pasture lands east of the Jordan (Jeremiah 50:19).
n.16: Yahweh answers the prayer of verse 14. *Them* is literally "him", that is, Israel. Some scholars read "Show us wonders", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.17: The question echoes Micah's own name, "Who is like Yahweh?" (1:1), and the song of Moses (Exodus 15:11). *Forgives wrongdoing* is literally "lifts guilt" (compare Exodus 34:7).
n.19: The Septuagint, the Syriac and the Vulgate read "our sins".
n.20: Literally "You will give truth to Jacob, faithful love to Abraham". Hebrew *emet*, "faithfulness, truth", and *chesed*, "faithful love", are the pair in Yahweh's description of himself in Exodus 34:6. Compare Genesis 22:16–18; 28:13–15.
